question.problem: In what direction does the function $g(x,y,z)=4{z}^{2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-y)$ increase most rapidly at the point $(2,-1,0)?$
question.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $g(x,y,z)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

So, we compute $∇g(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at the point $(2,-1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{z}^{2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-y)),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}(4{z}^{2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-y)),\,\frac{∂}{∂z}(4{z}^{2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-y))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{x-y},\,-\frac{2}{x-y},\,8z⟩ \\ ∇g(2,-1,0) & =⟨\frac{2}{2-(-1)},\,-\frac{2}{2-(-1)},\,8\cdot 0⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,-\frac{2}{3},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function increases most rapidly in the direction of $⟨\frac{2}{3},\,-\frac{2}{3},\,0⟩.$
